clue.text: American riders completely annoyed, having to return by taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
all means completely, as in 'all wrong'

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so this word is written backwards

parts.note: sore means annoyed or aggrieved

explanation.surface: Some American horsemen are furious at having to ride home in a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to return' turns SORE into EROS. 'by taxi' puts CAB beside the rest; the charade is written in answer order, so CAB goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballeros are horsemen of the Spanish-speaking Americas, from the Spanish word for a gentleman rider.

clue.text: State — Virginia — handed over by sovereign

indicators.note: handed over suggests turned over, so these letters are turned round

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A US state is passed into the hands of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun, given Virginia, but it is the verb 'declare'. 'handed over' turns VA into AV.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare firmly, a formal synonym of stating something.

clue.text: Empty apartment near centre of Heidelberg provides accommodation

parts.note: an apartment is a FLAT; empty, it has O (nothing) inside it

indicators.note: the centre of a ten-letter word is its middle two letters, here taken from Heidelberg

explanation.surface: An unoccupied flat near the middle of a German university town offers somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: The empty apartment is a flat with O, nothing, in it. The middle letters of Heidelberg, EL, follow ('near').
explanation.definitionFit: A floatel is a floating hotel, a vessel or platform used as living quarters, for oil-rig workers for example.

clue.text: One metal mouthpiece put on old horse for show

parts.note: ex- means former or old
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bit is the metal bar in a horse's mouth

explanation.surface: A bit goes in the mouth of an elderly horse being prepared for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like the animal but is slang for heroin; 'put on' means the mouthpiece comes after the old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibit is an item put on show, and to exhibit is to display.

clue.text: Big shot clergyman has to raise voice audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the pieces are spoken and the result is what they sound like

parts.note: a canon is a senior cathedral clergyman, and to bawl is to raise your voice; together they are said aloud

explanation.surface: An important churchman has to shout so that he can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big shot' looks like an important person, which suits the clergyman, but it is a large projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonball is the large round shot fired from a cannon, literally a big shot.

clue.text: Learner on trunk road in bother

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is written after it, so the learner comes second

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north-south trunk road, written AI
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver on a main road finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts L after AI. The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; 1 is written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, as in 'what ails you?', a verb close to bothering.

clue.text: Casually mention train finally leaves punctually

indicators.note: casually suggests carelessly thrown about, so these letters are mixed up
leaves means goes away, so that letter is removed
finally points to the final letter of the word train

explanation.surface: Someone remarks offhandedly that the last train is departing on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train finally' is N; 'leaves' takes it out of MENTION to give METIO, and 'Casually' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving on time means arriving at the scheduled moment, which is what punctually describes.

clue.text: Supplies shop with lines to be slightly reduced

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a kind of shop

indicators.note: slightly reduced means made a little shorter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper supplies goods and has to cut back the amount of text a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be slightly reduced' takes the last letter off VERSE to leave VERS; 'with' joins it to DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver goods is to supply them, so delivers and supplies are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Youngster absorbs musical work by largely mature band

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky young person
op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to mature is to grow

explanation.surface: A young person is captivated by a piece of music played by a band that is getting on a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' is a group of musicians, not a strip; 'by' is just a link joining the mature piece to the musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop group is a band playing popular music.

clue.text: Pound coin oddly left in drawer

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word coin

explanation.surface: Some money and odd coins have been left in a drawer of a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' and 'coin' look like money and 'drawer' like furniture, but a pound is an enclosure and a drawer is one who draws. 'oddly' gives CI from coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a tool for drawing, so it can be called a drawer, one that draws.

clue.text: Quantity of superior port

indicators.note: a quantity of something is some of it, so the answer is part of the following word

explanation.surface: An amount of fine fortified wine is being poured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the wine, but it is a harbour city, Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport, usually just called Rio.

clue.text: What recyclers of maps aim for, being green?

parts.note: a chart is a map, especially one used at sea
recyclers aim to use things again, to reuse them

explanation.surface: Environmentally minded people who recycle old maps are trying to be green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like ecologically minded, which suits the recyclers, but it is the colour. The words 'aim for' tell you what recyclers want: reuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a yellowish-green colour, named after the French liqueur.

clue.text: Stretch of river in which vessels moored?

indicators.note: boats moored in a river are held within it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of river where boats are tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' looks like boats, but they are cooking pans. 'in which' places them inside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide open stretch of land, sea or sky.

clue.text: Irksome back trouble among team

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a gang is a team of workers

indicators.note: back means the word goes backwards

parts.note: ill means trouble or harm, as in 'speak no ill'

explanation.surface: A painful back problem among the players is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back trouble' reads as a sore back, but 'back' only turns the word for trouble round before it goes among the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Something galling is vexing or irritating, the same as irksome.

clue.text: Gathering in front of room for somewhere to sleep

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering

explanation.surface: A gathering in front of a room where people sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering in' looks like a container, but 'in front of' only sets the order of the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorm, short for dormitory, is a room where several people sleep.

clue.text: Stubborn cook again to hold onto ham?

indicators.note: to hold onto something is to keep it inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: to refry is to fry a second time
a ham is a bad, overacting actor

explanation.surface: An obstinate cook has to reheat the ham once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like meat to cook, but it is an overacting performer, held inside the word for cooking again.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory means stubbornly unmanageable or resisting control.

clue.text: Copper leads force, following strike

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
F is the symbol for force in physics
f. is short for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A police officer leads the police force after a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, Cu; 'leads' puts it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff is to strike with an open hand, a blow around the head.

clue.text: We're told young male worker is very busy

indicators.note: we're told means the sound is what we hear, so the pieces are spoken

parts.note: a boy is a young male; the ant is the stock worker in crosswords, from worker ants

explanation.surface: Apparently a lad on a job has plenty on.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY and ANT run together and said out loud give the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant market or economy is one with plenty of activity, lively and busy.

clue.text: Maybe Spanish-speaking man in a recital, performing

indicators.note: performing suggests acting out or putting on a show, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish speaker might be the man performing in a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' means Spanish-speaking is one example; the answer is used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin American describes people from Central and South America, many of whom speak Spanish.

clue.text: What 'ospital is doing, 'opefully, in part of London

indicators.note: the dropped first letter shows the speaker drops the letter H

parts.note: a hospital is healing its patients

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding speaker says the hospital is healing patients, he hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped Hs in 'ospital and 'opefully show the H-dropping accent: HEALING said this way loses its H. Ealing is a borough in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a borough of west London, famous for its film studios.

clue.text: Intimidated girl got married, going after love

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, written O
Vera is a girl's name
wed means got married

explanation.surface: A girl got married after falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is the tennis score zero; 'going after' sets the girl and the wedding after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overawed means filled with awe to the point of being intimidated.

clue.text: Shake naughty child involved in struggle

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child shakes about in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shake' could be a noun, but here it is the verb; 'involved in' puts the child inside the struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to shake rapidly back and forth.

clue.text: Hustler acting like a fox without compassion

indicators.note: acting suggests playing a part or putting on a show, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: foxes are proverbially sly, cunning

explanation.surface: A con artist behaving with foxlike cunning shows no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hustler acting' reads as a con man performing, but 'acting' is the anagram signal; foxes are proverbially cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthlessly means doing something with no pity or mercy.

clue.text: Rise shortly after recruiting top insurgent writer

indicators.note: recruiting means taking people in, so one piece goes inside another
shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a hillock is a small rise in the ground
A1 means first-rate or top, written AI
a rebel is an insurgent

explanation.surface: An uprising quickly follows the enlisting of a leading rebel writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' looks like an uprising, but it is a small hill; 'shortly' drops its last letter and 'recruiting' takes the first-rate rebel inside. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French author, known for his Cautionary Tales for children.

clue.text: Venomous creature caught eating ostrich-like bird

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: copped is slang for caught
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird like an ostrich

explanation.surface: A dangerous animal is caught eating a large bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The ostrich-like bird is a South American runner; 'eating' puts it inside the slang word for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: The copperhead is a venomous North American snake.

clue.text: Scandinavian involved in exploit led by South African

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it
a Dane is someone from Denmark

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian caught up in a South African adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploit' looks like a noun, a feat, but it is the verb; 'led by' puts the South abbreviation first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese means from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Succeed fitting first of shelves inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: proper means fitting or appropriate

indicators.note: first of means take the first letter of the word shelves

explanation.surface: Shelving goes up first in a successful fit-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' could mean follow on, but here it means do well; 'inside' puts the shelf letter within the word for fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to succeed and do well.

clue.text: Luggage European lost in old Italian town

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so that letter is removed

parts.note: cases are luggage

explanation.surface: A European tourist's luggage is lost in an old Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes one E out of CASES to leave CASS. Cassino is the town below Monte Cassino, scene of a famous Second World War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassino is a town in central Italy, ancient Casinum, famous for its abbey and the 1944 battle.

clue.text: Old actor in send-up of Shakespeare's last two pieces

indicators.note: a send-up in a down clue lifts the letters upwards, so they read backwards
last two means the final two letters of the name Shakespeare

parts.note: gats are guns, slang pieces

explanation.surface: An elderly actor in a parody of Shakespeare's final plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'send-up' looks like a parody but turns RE (the last two letters of Shakespeare) and GATS, giving STAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran performer; stager alone means an experienced actor.

clue.text: Like part of breakfast Margaret hasn't started?

indicators.note: hasn't started means the first letter is missing

parts.note: Peggy is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret hasn't begun her breakfast yet.
explanation.walkthrough: PEGGY loses its first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggy means tasting of or covered in egg, like fried eggs at breakfast.
